heading: Group Visits, School Trips & Coach Parties
intro: Bring a group aboard the Manchester Ship Canal. Group rates on the City River Tour, or a private charter for schools, youth groups and the coach trade — all from Salford Quays.

sections.heading: Three ways to bring a group aboard
sections.note: Full group, school and trade details — TBC from Simon (content-checklist.md).

sections.heading: Group bookings (10+)
body: Bringing a group of ten or more? There are two easy ways aboard. Join a scheduled public sailing of our City River Tour at a group rate, or take a private charter of the whole boat for complete flexibility over your date, timings and route.

Public sailings suit sightseeing groups — social clubs, societies, community groups and work outings who want the tour itself. We reserve seats for your group together on a set departure. For full control of your date, timings and route, a private charter makes the vessel exclusively yours.
sections.note: Group discount rate, organiser-goes-free policy and payment terms — TBC from Simon (content-checklist.md).

sections.heading: School & youth groups
body: School trips, college groups, scouts, guides and youth organisations sail as a private charter — the whole boat is yours, not a shared public sailing. That means one group, a tailored commentary pitched to your age range, and simple logistics from boarding to disembarking.
We don’t offer party or prom bookings for school and college groups — our school charters are daytime educational visits.

The Ship Canal is a floating history lesson: the Industrial Revolution and the age of the docks, the working waterway that built the city, and the MediaCity regeneration that transformed it. It is a hands-on complement to the classroom — geography, history and local studies all on one route.
sections.note: Risk assessment documentation, teacher planning visits and adult-to-pupil ratio guidance — TBC from Simon (content-checklist.md).

sections.heading: Coach parties & tour operators
body: We welcome coach parties and tour operators aboard the City River Tour. Whether you are building a Manchester day out or slotting a river cruise into a wider itinerary, our sightseeing tour is an easy, memorable inclusion — around an hour on the water with live commentary.

Coaches can set down close to the Millennium Footbridge boarding point; we will advise on the nearest drop-off and parking when you book. Pre-booked group rates and invoice payment are available for the trade.

items.question: What is the minimum group size?
items.answer: Group rates apply to parties of 10 or more on a scheduled City River Tour; school, youth and other private charters take the whole boat. Exact minimums and boat capacity — TBC.

items.question: What happens if the weather is bad?
items.answer: The boat has a heated indoor cabin, so cruises run in most weather. If conditions affect sailing we contact the group organiser to rearrange. Full weather and cancellation policy — TBC.

items.question: Are groups accessible for wheelchair users and less mobile guests?
items.answer: Step-free boarding is available where tides allow, and we will talk through your group’s needs before you sail. Full accessibility details — TBC. See our Accessibility page.

items.question: How do deposits and payment work for groups?
items.answer: Group and charter bookings can be arranged with a deposit and balance, and invoice payment is available for schools and the trade. Deposit amounts and payment terms — TBC.

items.question: Can we have a tailored commentary or itinerary?
items.answer: Yes — private charters (including school and youth groups) can have commentary pitched to the group, and we can talk through timings and route. Confirmed when you book. (TBC)

items.question: Do group organisers or drivers go free?
items.answer: We plan to offer organiser and driver/courier-goes-free arrangements; the exact policy is being confirmed. (TBC)
